([[Fort Lauderdale, Florida]]) | draftteam = [[Detroit Pistons]] | draftyear = 2023 | draftround = 1 | draftpick = 5 | career_start = 2021 | career_end = | years1 = 2021–2022 | team1 = [[Overtime Elite|Team Elite]] | years2 = 2022–2023 | team2 = City Reapers | years3 = {{nbay|2023|start}}–present | team3 = [[Detroit Pistons]] | highlights = * [[NBA All-Defensive Team|NBA All-Defensive First Team]] ({{nbay|2025|end}}) * [[List of NBA annual steals leaders|NBA steals leader]] ({{nbay|2025|end}}) * 2× [[Overtime Elite|OTE]] Champion (2022, 2023) * 2× OTE Finals [[most valuable player|MVP]] (2022, 2023) * OTE Most Valuable Player (2023) * All-OTE First Team (2023) }} '''Ausar XLNC Thompson''' ({{IPAc-en|ə|ˈ|s|ɑːr|_|ˈ|ɛ|k|s|ə|l|ə|n|s|_|ˈ|t|ɒ|m|s|ə|n}} {{respelling|ə|SAR|_|EK|sə|lənss|_|TOM|sən}}; born January 30, 2003) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Detroit Pistons]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[high school basketball]] for [[Pine Crest School]] in [[Fort Lauderdale, Florida]], where he was rated a five-star [[College recruiting|recruit]] and won a state title alongside his twin brother [[Amen Thompson]]. He signed with [[List of developmental and minor sports leagues|development league]] [[Overtime Elite]] (OTE) out of high school; there, he won two straight OTE titles, earned Finals [[most valuable player|Most Valuable Player]] (MVP) twice, and was named league MVP in 2023. Thompson was selected fifth overall by the Pistons in the [[2023 NBA draft]]. He was the [[List of NBA annual steals leaders|NBA steals leader]] and made the [[NBA All-Defensive Team|NBA All-Defensive First Team]] in the [[2025–26 NBA season]]. ==Early life== Thompson was born to Maya Wilson and Troy Thompson and raised in [[San Leandro, California]].{{cite web |last=Gutierrez |first=Israel |title=The Thompson twins and Overtime Elite's unproven path to the NBA |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/34487913 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=January 26, 2023 |date=August 31, 2022}}{{cite web |last=Polacheck |first=Jacob |title=An Audacious Dream Meets Itself in Reality: A Look Inside Overtime Elite's Inaugural Season |url=https://www.zagsblog.com/2022/04/18/an-audacious-dream-meets-itself-in-reality-a-look-inside-overtime-elites-inaugural-season/ |publisher=Zagsblog |access-date=January 26, 2023 |date=April 18, 2022}} He is of Jamaican descent through his father.{{Cite web|url=https://thecaribbeancamera.com/twin-brothers-of-jamaican-heritage-make-history-in-nba-draft/|title=Twin brothers of Jamaican heritage make history in NBA draft|first=|last=|date=July 15, 2023|website=The Caribbean Camera}} His identical twin brother, [[Amen Thompson|Amen]], was born one minute before him; they share the middle name "XLNC" (pronounced "''excellence''").{{cite web |last=Graham |first=Pat |title=Twins Amen and Ausar Thompson set to be taken in top-10 of NBA draft |url=https://abcnews.go.com/Sports/wireStory/twins-amen-ausar-thompson-set-top-10-nba-100249856 |website=ABC News |access-date=May 26, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230623063213/https://abcnews.go.com/Sports/wireStory/twins-amen-ausar-thompson-set-top-10-nba-100249856 |archive-date=June 23, 2023 |date=June 20, 2023}} Thompson’s older brother, Troy Jr., played [[college basketball]] for [[Prairie View A&M Panthers basketball|Prairie View A&M]]. His uncle, [[Mark Thompson (hurdler)|Mark Thompson]], represented [[Jamaica]] in [[Athletics at the 1992 Summer Olympics – Men's 400 metres hurdles|400-meter hurdles]] at the [[1992 Summer Olympics]]. He and Amen began training for basketball under the guidance of their father by age seven and drew inspiration from [[LeBron James]]. The twins were [[homeschooled]] in sixth and seventh grades to focus on basketball. ==High school career== Entering eighth grade, Thompson and his family moved to [[Fort Lauderdale, Florida]] so that he and Amen could play high school basketball one year early at [[Pine Crest School]].{{cite web |last=Schoenfield |first=Bruce |title=The Teenagers Getting Six Figures to Leave Their High Schools for Basketball |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/11/30/magazine/overtime-elite-basketball-nba.html |website=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=January 26, 2023 |date=November 30, 2021}} The twins immediately started for the team.{{cite web |last=Wilson |first=David |title='I did not think we were going to win': Pine Crest wins state title with miracle comeback |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/high-school/prep-broward/article249715043.html |website=[[Miami Herald]] |access-date=January 27, 2023 |date=March 6, 2021}} As a sophomore, Thompson averaged 17.3 points, 6.3 rebounds and 2.6 assists per game, earning second-team All-[[Broward County, Florida|County]] honors. Entering his junior season, he was named to the Broward County Fab Five by the ''[[Sun Sentinel]]''.{{cite web |last=Lichtenstein |first=Adam |title=Broward County boys basketball Fab Five for 2020 (and the next five) |url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/highschool/basketball-boys/fl-sp-hs-boys-fab-five-broward-2020-20201215-xchw56365nft5kj73jym3z7uw4-story.html |website=[[Sun-Sentinel]] |access-date=January 27, 2023 |date=December 15, 2020}} Thompson averaged 22.6 points, 7.2 rebounds and 3.4 assists per game, helping his team win the Class 4A state championship. He shared Broward County Class 5A-1A co-player of the year with Amen.{{cite web |last=Lichtenstein |first=Adam |title=Broward 5A-1A boys basketball co-players of the year: Ausar Thompson and Amen Thompson, Pine Crest juniors |url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/highschool/all-county/fl-sp-ss-prem-ac-br-bhoop-small-poy-20210328-qjyzjbndyndqpksczpjufut46q-story.html |website=[[Sun-Sentinel]] |access-date=January 27, 2023 |date=March 27, 2021}} ===Recruiting=== Thompson was rated a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[ESPN]] and [[Rivals.com|Rivals]].{{cite web |title=Ausar Thompson – Basketball Recruiting |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/243381 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=June 18, 2023}}{{cite web |title=Ausar Thompson |url=https://n.rivals.com/content/athletes/ausar-thompson-260429?view=pv |publisher=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=June 18, 2023}} He gained interest from college programs in 2019, receiving a scholarship offer from [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]].{{cite web |last=Young |first=Justin |title=South Florida's Thompson Twins are catching on with recruiters |url=https://hoopseen.com/news/player/201910/south-floridas-thompson-twins-are-catching-recruiters |publisher=HoopSeen |access-date=January 27, 2023 |date=October 2, 2019}} Following his junior year, Thompson held offers from [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]], [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]], [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]], [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State]] and [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], among other programs, before deciding to not play [[college basketball]].{{cite web |last=Branham |first=Travis |date=May 26, 2021 |title=Elite twins Amen and Ausar Thompson skip college to join the Overtime Elite program |url=https://247sports.com/college/basketball/recruiting/Article/Amen-Thompson-Ausar-Thompson-commitment-Overtime-Elite-professional-pro-route-165746766/ |access-date=June 27, 2023 |publisher=[[247Sports]]}} ==Professional career== ===Team Elite (2021–2022)=== On May 25, 2021, Thompson signed a two-year contract with [[Overtime Elite]] (OTE), a new professional league based in [[Atlanta]] with players between ages 16 and 20. He joined the league with his brother Amen, bypassing his final year of high school and college.{{cite web |last=Boone |first=Kyle |title=Overtime Elite lands another set of twins as Amen and Ausar Thompson choose professional program over college |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/overtime-elite-lands-another-set-of-twins-as-amen-and-ausar-thompson-choose-professional-program-over-college/ |work=[[CBS Sports]] |access-date=January 28, 2023 |date=May 25, 2021}}{{cite magazine |last=Woo |first=Jeremy |title=Can Overtime Elite Disrupt Basketball With ... Twins? |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2022/03/07/overtime-elite-thompson-twins-daily-cover |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=January 28, 2023 |date=March 7, 2022}} In the 2021–22 season, Thompson played for Team Elite, one of three teams in the league, and averaged 14.7 points, 8.2 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 2.2 blocks per game.{{cite web |last=Araiza |first=Robert |title=Amen & Ausar Thompson: Should the San Antonio Spurs roll the dice? |url=https://airalamo.com/posts/amen-ausar-thompson-should-san-antonio-spurs-roll-dice/2 |publisher=Air Alamo |agency=[[FanSided]]|access-date=June 18, 2023 |date=January 13, 2023}}{{cite web |last=Sprung |first=Shlomo |title=Overtime Elite Roster 2022–23 |url=https://boardroom.tv/overtime-elite-roster-2022-23/ |publisher=Boardroom |access-date=June 18, 2023 |date=August 26, 2022}} He competed against other OTE teams, as well as [[College-preparatory school|prep-school]] and [[Postgraduate year|postgraduate]] opponents.{{cite web |last=Givony |first=Jonathan |date=October 13, 2021 |title=Overtime Elite announces 2021-22 schedule, roster for inaugural season |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/32381206 |access-date=January 28, 2023 |publisher=[[ESPN]]}} He led his team to the league championship and was named Finals MVP after recording 20 points and 11 rebounds in a 52–45 win over Team OTE in the decisive third game of the finals.{{cite web |last=Feldman |first=Joseph |title=Team Elite Wins First Overtime Elite Championship |url=https://overtimeelite.com/articles/b82a7362-6679-4e97-be6a-bf55e3294708 |publisher=[[Overtime Elite]] |access-date=June 18, 2023 |date=March 14, 2022}} Thompson played for OTE affiliate Team Overtime in [[The Basketball Tournament 2022|The Basketball Tournament]] in July 2022. His team lost to Omaha Blue Crew, 74–70, in the first round of the tournament.{{cite web |last=DeMarinis |first=Matt |title=Omaha Blue Crew outlasts Team Overtime in a battle of old versus new |url=https://whiteandbluereview.com/omaha-blue-crew-outlasts-team-overtime-in-a-battle-of-old-versus-new/ |publisher=White and Blue Review |access-date=January 28, 2021 |date=July 17, 2022}} ===City Reapers (2022–2023)=== In the 2022–23 OTE season, Thompson was named [[Captain (sports)|captain]] of the City Reapers and played alongside Amen.{{cite web |last=Feldman |first=Joseph |title=OTE Announces Roster Reveal and Expansion for Season 2 |url=https://overtimeelite.com/articles/d8ad12ca-acbd-44d1-b6d9-9f5f1c5def45 |publisher=[[Overtime Elite]] |access-date=June 18, 2023 |date=September 21, 2022}} On December 12, 2022, he earned league Player of the Week honors.{{cite web |last=Feldman |first=Joseph |title=Ausar Thompson Named Player of the Week |url=https://overtimeelite.com/articles/d075e871-2cfc-4b16-a41b-f14ceafa559d |publisher=[[Overtime Elite]] |access-date=June 18, 2023 |date=December 12, 2022}} Thompson was selected as Player of the Week for a second time on February 6, 2023, after posting a league single-game record 12 assists, with 17 points and eight rebounds in 21 minutes against the Holy Rams.{{cite web |last=Feldman |first=Joseph |title=Ausar Thompson Named OTE Player of the Week |url=https://overtimeelite.com/articles/6fdd1cc4-30ba-4a40-be5f-33dd9681a473 |publisher=[[Overtime Elite]] |access-date=June 18, 2023 |date=February 6, 2023}} At the end of the regular season, he was named OTE MVP and made the All-OTE First Team, with averages of 16.3 points, 7.1 rebounds, 6.1 assists and 2.4 steals per game.{{cite web |last=Cobb |first=David |title=2023 NBA Draft: Amen, Ausar Thompson declare as likely lottery picks after playing for Overtime Elite |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/2023-nba-draft-amen-ausar-thompson-declare-as-likely-lottery-picks-after-playing-for-overtime-elite/ |work=[[CBS Sports]] |access-date=June 18, 2023 |date=April 21, 2023}}{{cite web |last=Feldman |first=Joseph |title=OTE Announces Regular Season Awards |url=https://overtimeelite.com/articles/b66abb33-0079-4dc0-9858-7f6933f9a54a |publisher=[[Overtime Elite]] |access-date=June 18, 2023 |date=February 20, 2023}} Thompson led the Reapers to the league title in a 3–0 [[Whitewash (sport)|sweep]] of the YNG Dreamerz, repeating as Finals MVP. In the final game, he made a game-winning three-pointer with three seconds left.{{cite web |last=Feldman |first=Joseph |title=City Reapers Win OTE Championship |url=https://overtimeelite.com/articles/81ad0922-4800-435b-9706-a5a6180ceb56 |publisher=[[Overtime Elite]] |access-date=June 18, 2023 |date=March 7, 2023}} On April 21, 2023, he declared for the [[2023 NBA draft]], where analysts viewed him as a potential top-10 pick. ===Detroit Pistons (2023–present)=== The [[Detroit Pistons]] selected Thompson with the fifth overall pick in the [[2023 NBA draft]], one pick behind his twin brother Amen.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/ausar-thompson-pistons-no-5-pick-2023-nba-draft|title=Ausar Thompson: Meet the Pistons' No. 5 pick in 2023 NBA Draft|website=ClutchPoints|last=Siegel|first=Brett|date=June 22, 2023|access-date=June 22, 2023}} They were the first brothers in NBA draft history to be selected in the top five in the same year.{{Cite web |last=Woodyard |first=Eric |date=June 23, 2023 |title=Amen, Ausar Thompson first brothers taken in top five of same NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com.au/nba/story?id=37902522 |access-date=June 27, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}} On October 25, 2023, Thompson made his NBA regular-season debut, putting up four points, seven rebounds, three assists and five blocks in a 103–102 loss to the [[Miami Heat]]. Thompson also became the youngest player in NBA history to put up at least five blocks in an NBA debut, at 20 years old and 269 days.{{cite web |last=Pagaduan |first=Jedd |date=October 25, 2023 |title=Pistons wing Ausar Thompson smashes Shawn Bradley's rookie record with scary defense vs. Heat |url=https://clutchpoints.com/pistons-news-ausar-thompson-smashes-shawn-bradleys-rookie-record-with-scary-defense-vs-heat |access-date=October 25, 2023 |website=ClutchPoints}} Thompson was a part of the roster that lost an NBA record-high 28 straight games in the 2023–24 season. He played in 63 games (38 starts) during his rookie season, averaging 8.8 points, 6.4 rebounds and 1.9 assists. On March 20, 2024, Thompson was shut down for the season after being treated for a [[thrombus|blood clot]].{{Cite web |last=Sam |first=Doric |date=March 20, 2024 |title=Pistons' Ausar Thompson Will Miss Rest of 2023-24 NBA Season for Blood Clot Treatment |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10113809-pistons-ausar-thompson-will-miss-rest-of-2023-24-nba-season-for-blood-clot-treatment |access-date=March 20, 2024 |website=[[Bleacher Report]] |language=en}} In 2025 he played in the playoffs for the first time. During the [[2025–26 NBA season]], Thompson enjoyed a more regular starting role with the Pistons. He finished the season as the NBA leader in steals and came 3rd in [[NBA Defensive Player of the Year |Defensive Player of the Year award]] voting while also earning himself an [[NBA All-Defensive Team|NBA All-Defensive First Team]] selection.{{cite web |title=Spurs' Victor Wembanyama named 2025-26 Kia NBA Defensive Player of the Year |url=https://www.nba.com/news/kia-nba-defensive-player-of-the-year-award-2025-26 |website=NBA.com |publisher=Tim Reynolds |date=April 20, 2026}}{{Cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2025-26-all-defensive-teams-announced |title=Kia All-Defensive Teams, NBA Social Justice Champion revealed live on Peacock |website=NBA.com |date=May 22, 2026}} ==Career
